main_body: Three-storey red brick building with a flat grey stone-paved roof, a cream cornice, a facade of windows with sills and lintels, and an arched green double door.
top_band: Light lilac-grey speckled paving slab with a lighter parapet edge, rows ~2-39, then a cream cornice at rows ~41-46
evidence: In a centre column I read a light parapet/edge at rows 38-40, a cream cornice at rows 41-46 and a dark brown shadow row at about row 47. Below that is the brick face with window sills, lintels and a door arch. The flat roof is clearly drawn from above as a wide horizontal surface with tile joints and rooftop vents. The windows have dark inner frames and sills, so they read as inset. The roof is tall for a foreshortened top, but it is a real horizontal surface and the front face is also fully drawn.

style.evidence: The brick has several red-brown tones with mortar rows and per-brick variation. The cream trim has 3-4 tones. The roof slab carries speckle and joint lines in about 4 greys. The outlines are dark maroon next to brick and a darker grey next to stone, not black. The windows add blue glass with highlights and white frames, and the door has an arched fanlight and handles. Tile density is high and holds up against the reference houses. The roof is large and fairly uniform, but its speckle keeps it from reading as a flat fill.
